title: Cannabis Simple Syrup: How to Make THC Syrup
h1: Cannabis-Infused Simple Syrup That Actually Infuses
metaDescription: A cannabis simple syrup that really works: a glycerin or tincture method, since THC barely dissolves in sugar water, plus dose math and fridge storage.
excerpt: THC barely dissolves in sugar water, so simmering flower in syrup leaves most of it behind. Use vegetable glycerin or a measured tincture instead, and do the math.
keyTakeaways: THC barely dissolves in water: about 2.8 mg per liter at room temperature.
It does dissolve in alcohol, oils and glycerin, and glycerin mixes smoothly into syrup.
Divide the total THC by the teaspoons of syrup you made, and shake before every use.
Store the syrup in the fridge in a bottle labeled with the date and strength.
body:
A good cannabis simple syrup sweetens coffee, tea, lemonade and mocktails with a dose you can count by the teaspoon. The catch: simmering flower in sugar water barely works. Here's why, plus two methods that do.

## Why plain sugar water falls short

| Liquid | Does THC dissolve in it? |
|---|---|
| Water | Barely: about 2.8 mg per liter |
| Alcohol | Readily |
| Oils and fats | Readily |
| Glycerin | Yes, and glycerin mixes with water |

So simmered sugar water leaves most of the THC in the plant matter you strain out, while glycerin carries THC into a water-based syrup.

## How to dose cannabis simple syrup

Divide the total THC by the teaspoons of syrup. For the glycerin method, 1.75 grams of 20% flower holds at most 350 mg; in about 2 cups (96 teaspoons) that's under 4 mg per teaspoon, and real numbers run lower. With a tincture, use the label: 100 mg in 1 1/2 cups (72 teaspoons) is about 1.4 mg per teaspoon. Shake before each use, start with one teaspoon and wait 2 hours.

## Two methods that work

### Glycerin method

Along with sugar and water, you need food-grade vegetable glycerin and decarbed flower ([how to decarb](/blog/cannabis-decarboxylation/)). Warm the flower in the glycerin over very low heat for 2 to 3 hours without letting it simmer. Strain, then stir the infused glycerin into cooled syrup.

### Tincture method

Make the syrup, let it cool completely, and whisk in a measured amount of THC tincture. Alcohol- and glycerin-based tinctures blend in; oil-based ones float. Our [tincture guide](/blog/cannabis-tincture-guide/) explains the types, and you can check [your store's menu](/shop/) for options, since selection varies by store.

## Storage and labeling

Bottle the syrup, label it with the date and estimated mg per teaspoon, and refrigerate it where kids and pets can't reach. Poison control is 1-800-222-1222.

## Ways to use it

Stir a measured teaspoon into coffee, iced tea or our [strawberry canna-nade](/blog/frozen-strawberry-canna-nade/). Blend it into slushies, or add a counted number of teaspoons to a popsicle base and divide by the molds, as in our [infused popsicles](/blog/cannabis-infused-popsicles/). It can also replace part of the sugar syrup in homemade marshmallows cut into equal squares.

For adults 21 and older. Enjoy it responsibly.

faq.q: How strong is homemade cannabis syrup?
faq.a: As strong as your math says, at most. For glycerin syrup, multiply grams of flower by 1,000 and by the THC percentage, divide by the teaspoons of syrup, and expect less. With a tincture, the label gives the mg you add. A few mg per teaspoon keeps one spoonful modest.

faq.q: How long does infused syrup last?
faq.a: Plan on about a month in the fridge in a clean, sealed bottle. Shake it before each use, since the infusion can settle. Toss it if it turns cloudy, smells off or shows mold, and keep the label current with the batch date and strength.

faq.q: Can I use it in hot drinks?
faq.a: Yes. Stir a measured teaspoon into coffee or tea just as you would plain syrup; a warm drink doesn't change the dose. Plan on the usual edible wait of up to 2 hours before deciding on more, and keep track of how many teaspoons you've had.

recipe.yield: About 2 cups (glycerin method) or 1 1/2 cups (tincture method)
ingredients: Glycerin method: 1/2 cup food-grade vegetable glycerin
Tincture method: a THC tincture, alcohol- or glycerin-based, measured to your dose
steps: For the syrup, bring the water and both sugars to a simmer, stirring until dissolved. Cool completely.
Glycerin method: decarb the flower on a lined tray in a 240°F oven for 30 to 40 minutes, then cool it and break it up.
Warm the flower in the glycerin over very low heat, in a double boiler or a slow cooker on low, for 2 to 3 hours. Keep it below a simmer and stir now and then.
Strain through a fine sieve lined with cheesecloth, pressing gently, and stir the infused glycerin into the cooled syrup.
Tincture method: whisk the measured tincture into the cooled syrup until evenly mixed.
Bottle, label with the date and estimated mg per teaspoon, and refrigerate. Shake before each use.
recipe.dosingNote: These are estimates. Glycerin example: 1.75 g of flower at 20% THC = 1.75 × 1,000 × 0.20 = 350 mg at most, and 350 ÷ 96 teaspoons ≈ 3.6 mg per teaspoon at most. Tincture example: 100 mg ÷ 72 teaspoons ≈ 1.4 mg per teaspoon. For the glycerin version, the real figure depends on your flower's actual potency and on what decarboxylation and the infusion lose, so expect less. Start with one teaspoon and wait at least 2 hours before having more. Label the bottle and keep it away from children and pets.

review.summary: 16 claims checked: 16 ok, 0 fixed. The solubility table matches PubChem, the decarb setting matches Wang 2016, the dose and yield math hold, and the tincture line points to the store menu without saying any product is stocked.

claims.source: https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/16078 (PUG View, Solubility): 'In water, 2.8 mg/L at 23 °C'; 'Essentially insoluble in water'

claims.claim: THC dissolves readily in alcohol and in oils and fats, and also in glycerin (table, takeaway)
claims.source: PubChem CID 16078: '1 part in 1 part of alcohol ... 1 part in 3 parts of glycerol'; 'Soluble in fixed oils.'

claims.claim: Glycerin mixes with water, so it carries THC into a water-based syrup (table, takeaway, body)
Simmering flower in sugar water leaves most of the THC in the plant matter (excerpt, body)
claims.source: arithmetic on PubChem's 2.8 mg/L: about 2 cups (0.47 L) of water can hold roughly 1.3 mg dissolved, against about 350 mg in 1.75 g of 20% flower

claims.claim: Alcohol- and glycerin-based tinctures blend into syrup; oil-based ones float
claims.source: PubChem CID 753: glycerol 'Miscible with ethanol', 'Solubility in water: miscible', 'Insoluble in fixed and volatile oils' (oil does not mix into the water-glycerin syrup)

claims.claim: Glycerin dose math: 1.75 g x 1,000 x 0.20 = 350 mg at most; 2 cups = 96 teaspoons; 350 / 96 = about 3.6 mg (under 4 mg) per teaspoon (body, FAQ, dosing note)

claims.claim: Tincture dose math: 100 mg in 1 1/2 cups (72 teaspoons) = about 1.4 mg per teaspoon
Yield: about 2 cups (glycerin method) or 1 1/2 cups (tincture method)
claims.source: estimate: 1 cup water and 1 cup sugar make about 1 1/2 cups of syrup; the glycerin method adds 1/2 cup of glycerin, less what the strained flower keeps

claims.claim: Decarb the flower at 240°F for 30 to 40 minutes
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC): 'the concentration of THCA-A approached zero in 30, 9, and 6 min at 110°C, 130°C, and 145°C, respectively' (240°F is about 116°C)

claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/health-effects/poisoning.html (WebFetch): 'Take from 30 minutes to 2 hours to feel intoxicating effects.'

review.notes: Independent fact-check: PubChem solubility sections for THC (CID 16078) and glycerol (CID 753) read through PUG View; Wang 2016 full text through Europe PMC; CDC page opened with WebFetch; syrup shelf life confirmed by WebSearch (MasterClass, which refuses WebFetch). High Society appears once: check your store's menu for tinctures, since selection varies by store (hs-facts lists tinctures on two store menus only). Writer's notes: The brief corrects the flower-simmered-in-sugar-water method; it is never presented as the infusion. Glycerin is not claimed to extract better or worse than alcohol or fat (no source found), only that the glycerin figure is a ceiling. Tinctures are named generically; the menu link says selection varies by store (hs-facts lists tinctures on only two store menus). Cocktails are not suggested. FAQ idea "Is THC water-soluble?" is answered by the solubility section and table.
